name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,632

clue.text: Son horsing about with grandpa makes bloomer

indicators.note: horsing about is fooling around boisterously, so the letters romp out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy is larking about with his grandfather, and the result is an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' reads as a gaffe, but here it means a plant that blooms; the son and grandpa together are shuffled into SNAPDRAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapdragon is a garden flowering plant, and anything that flowers can jokingly be called a bloomer.

clue.text: In the sack, husband hot for booty

indicators.note: things placed in a receptacle end up inside it, so the following pieces go within

blocks.note: to hit the sack is to go to bed
H is the abbreviation for husband
something hot is fashionable, or in

explanation.surface: A racy picture of a husband getting amorous in bed, eager for some booty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the sack' looks like a phrase meaning in bed, and it nearly is: the sack is BED, which holds H and IN, giving BEHIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Booty is slang for the buttocks, and behind is an everyday word for the same body part.

clue.text: On a drug, coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone high on a drug finds its effects starting to kick in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a drug' reads as one phrase, but 'On' is the definition and only the drug is turned upwards, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop is a preposition meaning on top of, so it can replace on in a phrase like on the table.

clue.text: Junkie right to punch church leader

indicators.note: a punch lands inside its target, so one piece is driven into another

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
OK means all right, correct
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: An addict is quite justified in thumping the head of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church leader' looks like one phrase meaning a bishop, but church is CE, punched by OK, and leader stands alone as HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A cokehead is slang for someone addicted to cocaine, a particular kind of junkie.

clue.text: To me, the Indy crossword editor is a stud

definitions.text: To me, the Indy crossword editor

blocks.clueFragment: To me, the Indy crossword editor
blocks.note: first meaning: to a setter, the puzzle editor is the person in charge
second meaning: a raised knob or ornamental stud

explanation.surface: The setter cheekily praises the Independent's puzzle editor as a ladies' man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stud' tempts as a womaniser, but it is a decorative knob on a shield or ceiling; the setter is the 'me' whose editor is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Your employer or supervisor is your boss, and a boss is also a round raised ornament or knob.

clue.text: Happy prisoner with outdoor accommodation

blocks.note: con is short for convict
a tent is shelter for camping outdoors

explanation.surface: A convict is cheerful about being housed outdoors under canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is a standard shortening of convict, and the shelter is just a camping tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Content is an adjective for being satisfied and at ease, a close synonym of happy.

clue.text: Centenarian leader and topless coquette don't do it any more!

indicators.note: the leader is at the front, so only the opening letter is kept
without a top, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of the word
a coquette is a flirt, or tease

explanation.surface: Someone tells a hundred-year-old and a half-naked flirt to stop their antics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centenarian leader' looks like an elderly chief, but only the first letter is taken; the tease loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Cease is an imperative meaning stop, so it stands for the exclamation telling someone to quit an action.

clue.text: Old joke about bit of zombifying gas

indicators.note: a bit is a small part, here just the opening letter
about means around, so these letters surround another

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
as in 'that's a good one'
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tired gag about a gas that turns people into zombies.
explanation.walkthrough: O and ONE together wrap round the Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen, a gas found in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Chart-topping book written about love, perhaps

indicators.note: about means turned round, so everything before reads the other way

blocks.note: a chart-topping record is No 1
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A bestselling book has been penned on the subject of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: No 1 is written with the digit as the letter I; NO I and TOME together are turned round to give EMOTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is one example of a strong feeling, and 'perhaps' signals that it is an instance of the wider category.

clue.text: Nag Republican to wear headgear

indicators.note: a wearer is inside what they wear, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
a cap is a hat

explanation.surface: Pestering a Republican politician into putting on a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' could be a horse, but here it is the verb to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain persistently and fussily, the same as to nag.

clue.text: Naughty promises in burlesque?

indicators.note: naughty letters misbehave and refuse to stay in line

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Saucy promises made on stage in a striptease show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word placing promises inside burlesque, but it is part of the fodder; burlesque here means parody, not striptease.
explanation.definitionFit: An impression is a comic imitation of a person, and burlesque is mocking parody, so the question mark marks one example.

clue.text: Man with hens, possibly in Scottish region?

blocks.note: he is a male pronoun
a hen party is held for a bride-to-be, so brides are hens

explanation.surface: A man surrounded by chickens, perhaps on a farm somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Hens are not birds: a hen night is the British bachelorette party, and the bride is the hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are island groups off Scotland's west coast, forming a recognised area of the country.

clue.text: Censure son getting in after the agreed time

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son

blocks.clueFragment: getting in after the agreed time
blocks.note: arriving after the agreed time is being late

explanation.surface: A parent tells off a son who came home past his curfew.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase about coming home is one block, a definition of being late.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate is British informal for criticising harshly, which is to censure.

clue.text: Sexy books found in Morecambe?

indicators.note: what is found in something sits inside it

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
Eric Morecambe was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: Racy reading material discovered in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a Lancashire resort, but here it is the comedian Eric Morecambe, so it stands for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic describes something arousing sexual desire, a close synonym of sexy.

clue.text: Where one might find a satellite dish for free?

definitions.text: Where one might find a satellite dish

blocks.clueFragment: Where one might find a satellite dish
blocks.note: first meaning: a satellite dish is usually mounted on a building's roof or wall
second meaning: a phrase for drinks or food given by the establishment without charge

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a question about free TV dishes; the first half is a literal location, the second the idiom for a free round.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something given by a bar or restaurant without charge, while literally the phrase locates something on a building.

clue.text: Water pipe knight installed in toilet

indicators.note: something installed in a place is fitted inside it

blocks.note: N is knight in chess notation
bog is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A plumbing job: a water pipe fitted by a knight in the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water pipe' sounds like plumbing but is the smoking device; a bog is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bong is a smoking device that draws smoke through water, which is literally a water pipe.

clue.text: For the most part, work fast to get rich

indicators.note: most but not all of the word survives, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: an opus is a work of art or music
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Advice that working quickly is mostly the way to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed but is the noun for going without food, here the season of Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy and lavish, showing great riches, so it fits rich.

clue.text: A charge or payment?

blocks.note: taken as written
a person placed in someone's care is their charge

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a sum demanded is a fee or a reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a fee, setting up a money theme with payment, but it is a person placed in someone's care, a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a sum granted, as in a pay award or damages, so it is a kind of payment.

clue.text: Secretary going around with little desire for sex?

indicators.note: going around means turning about, so the word faces the other way

blocks.note: a PA is a personal assistant
petite means small

explanation.surface: An office secretary goes about with hardly any interest in romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little desire' reads as low libido, but little is a separate piece and desire belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is a natural craving, and sexual appetite is a common phrase, so the question mark marks one example.

clue.text: Swimmer, after split, ahead on the turn!

indicators.note: once split, a single word breaks into two words read side by side
turning means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: split into 'a head', and nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: A swimmer, having made a break for it, is leading at the turn of the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' sounds like breaking away in a race, but it tells you to split the word 'ahead' into two.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuna is a large ocean fish, and swimmer is a common crossword term for any fish.

clue.text: Become religious after knocking over veggie

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the word goes the other way

blocks.note: to turn is to become, as in turn sour
pi is short for pious

explanation.surface: Someone finds God after toppling over a vegetarian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veggie' looks like a vegetarian, but it is short for a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a root vegetable, and veggie is informal shorthand for vegetable.

clue.text: High-flyer with ego we all knocked about

indicators.note: being knocked about is being battered around, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An arrogant high achiever whom everyone has roughed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' suggests an ambitious go-getter, but here it is literally a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle owl is a large owl, a bird that flies high, so it is literally a high-flyer.

clue.text: Dope shot in group of quite high people

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information, as is dope
a shot is an attempt

explanation.surface: Drugs injected at a party of rather stoned people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' and 'high' set up a drugs scene, but dope is information and high means of social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the class just below the nobility, people of fairly elevated social standing.

clue.text: Clubs which are somewhat smaller than Forest?

blocks.note: first meaning: golf clubs with large heads used for long shots
second meaning: areas of trees, smaller than a forest

explanation.surface: Comparing football clubs, some lesser than Nottingham Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital F makes it look like Nottingham Forest, an English football club, but it is just a large expanse of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf drivers were traditionally wooden-headed clubs, and stands of trees smaller than a forest are woodland.

clue.text: Hiker's nothing much to write home about

definitions.text: nothing much to write home about

blocks.note: first meaning: someone travelling on foot

blocks.clueFragment: nothing much to write home about
blocks.note: second meaning: dull and uninspired

explanation.surface: A rambler shrugs that their walk was not very exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiker's' reads as possessive but is 'hiker is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A walker on foot is a pedestrian, and the adjective describes something ordinary and lacking any excitement.

clue.text: School nurse taking temperature close to lido

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside
the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter counts

blocks.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse
T is the abbreviation for temperature
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A school nurse checks children's temperatures near the open-air pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School nurse' reads as one job title, but School is the definition; Eton is the famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English public school, the most common crossword school.

clue.text: Is Hoskins upset by male religious leader?

indicators.note: upset means overturned, which in a down entry flips the letters

blocks.note: Hoskins is the setter, so the question becomes 'am I?'
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: The setter asks whether he is offended by a male cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for 'I', and a question puts the verb first.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the man who leads prayers in a mosque, a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: Smell repelled old European, one with wind

indicators.note: what is repelled is driven back, so the word turns backwards

blocks.note: BO is body odour
O is the abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An elderly European with flatulence drives everyone away with the stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' suggests flatulence, but it means a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument, so it is a thing played with breath, cheekily called wind.

clue.text: Slice of Urda wrapped in red fish

indicators.note: a slice is a small piece, here just the opening letter
what is wrapped sits inside its wrapping

blocks.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a left-wing red
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cut of cheese parcelled up with red fish like salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: Urda is a whey cheese, but only its first letter matters; 'red fish' looks like one phrase, but red is the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a freshwater fish related to salmon.

clue.text: A support that's held in extremely rebellious busts

indicators.note: what is held in is enclosed, so one piece sits inside another
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only outer letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
outer letters of the word
a rest is a support, as in an armrest

explanation.surface: A brassiere that keeps very unruly bosoms under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' and 'busts' suggest a bra, but busts are police raids or arrests.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust is slang for an arrest by police, so plural busts are arrests.
